origin_detail: Post-release audit found memory and deferred NetCDF behavior need comparable evidence
scientific_problem: Equivalent scientific selections must produce equivalent values and metadata
computational_problem: Materialized and bounded reads can diverge in indexing, missingness, or attributes
why_oceancube: Backend correctness is a core cube responsibility
implementation_strategy: Define operation-by-operation parity fixtures and tolerances
notes: Parity measurement precedes backend expansion

origin_detail: No formal benchmark suite exists
scientific_problem: Users need predictable bounded operations on ocean cubes
computational_problem: Runtime regressions are invisible without reproducible size classes
why_oceancube: Performance is part of storage-aware cube behavior
implementation_strategy: Benchmark representative crop, slice, extract, collect, temporal, and geometry paths
prerequisites: Backend parity and fixture size classes
notes: Baseline first; optimization is not required for gate completion

origin_detail: Example-based tests do not cover broad coordinate and shape combinations
scientific_problem: Cube transformations must preserve dimensions, coordinates, units, and provenance invariants
computational_problem: Combinatorial shapes and selections are expensive to enumerate manually
why_oceancube: Contract invariants belong with the cube engine
implementation_strategy: Generate bounded valid/invalid cubes and assert algebraic and metadata properties
dependency_strategy: Development-only tool or internal generators; decision after prototype
notes: Includes singleton dimensions, reversed selections, and backend equivalence

origin_detail: No formal coverage baseline exists
scientific_problem: Critical scientific branches need visible test evidence
computational_problem: Raw percentages can hide untested error and metadata paths
why_oceancube: Package maintainers own test completeness
implementation_strategy: Measure by module and classify uncovered scientific, backend, error, and documentation paths
notes: Coverage is evidence, not a percentage-only gate

origin_detail: Materialization and large outputs need measured memory behavior
scientific_problem: Ocean fields can exceed available memory
computational_problem: Copies, array reshaping, and plotting can multiply peak allocation
why_oceancube: Storage-aware behavior is part of oceancube
implementation_strategy: Profile representative operations and compare estimates with peak allocations
dependency_strategy: Development-only profiler; no runtime dependency until justified
notes: Required before large 3-D and chunk planning

origin_detail: No formal stress suite exists
scientific_problem: Long time axes, sparse selections, and many variables expose backend edge cases
computational_problem: File handles, read plans, and memory pressure fail outside unit-scale fixtures
why_oceancube: Backend reliability belongs in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Add bounded opt-in stress profiles with recorded machine and data size
dependency_strategy: Development-only; exclude heavy runs from ordinary CI
notes: CI uses small representatives; scheduled/local runs may be larger

origin_detail: Real products are needed without committing operational datasets
scientific_problem: Scientific metadata and grid behavior must be tested against actual products
computational_problem: Large, credentialed, or restricted sources are not CI-safe
why_oceancube: Package validation needs governed representative evidence
implementation_strategy: Require source, license, derivation, checksum, size budget, and CI eligibility manifests
dependency_strategy: Provider clients remain outside core unless separately approved
notes: No download occurs in roadmap phase

proposed_api: ocean_cube descriptor input vs read_nc mode vs candidate cube_open()
origin_detail: read_nc materializes while a bounded deferred backend exists internally
scientific_problem: Users need explicit access to bounded reads without breaking read_nc compatibility
computational_problem: A public entry must preserve serialization, file identity, errors, and lifecycle
why_oceancube: NetCDF access is core oceancube I/O
implementation_strategy: Write API option paper and prototype internally before selecting a public surface
dependency_strategy: tidync is inspiration or oracle; not an automatic dependency
prerequisites: Backend parity baseline and provenance v1
notes: No function name is approved

proposed_api: schema fields and internal append/validate engine
origin_detail: Current provenance exists without an explicit schema version
scientific_problem: Scientific transformations need reproducible method and source lineage
computational_problem: Heterogeneous free-form records cannot be compared or migrated safely
why_oceancube: Every field transformation must record provenance
implementation_strategy: Define schema_version, operation, parameters, parents, source identity, time, package version, backend, coordinate transforms, and method ID
dependency_strategy: Native minimal schema first; CF integration in 0.3.0-B
prerequisites: Stable operation inventory and backend parity
notes: P0 minimal schema; extensible without serializing live backends

origin_detail: Current workflows target Copernicus Marine model products
scientific_problem: Validate depth, masks, variables, time, units, and real CF metadata
computational_problem: Authenticated access and product size prevent direct CI download
why_oceancube: Representative model data validates the primary ocean-cube use case
implementation_strategy: Derive a tiny checksum-pinned subset only after terms and redistribution review
dependency_strategy: No provider client added to core by this row
notes: CI-safe only if redistribution is approved; otherwise use metadata plus synthetic analogue

origin_detail: Independent public gridded source broadens provider evidence
scientific_problem: Validate rectilinear surface fields and long time axes
computational_problem: Stable version pinning and subset derivation are required
why_oceancube: Provider-independent behavior is a cube contract requirement
implementation_strategy: Select one public product and derive a tiny attributed subset
notes: Prefer a stable documented product rather than a live endpoint in CI

origin_detail: Surface products need quality and singleton-depth evidence
scientific_problem: Validate singleton depth, flags, packed values, missingness, and geolocation
computational_problem: Provider encodings and redistribution conditions vary
why_oceancube: Satellite surfaces are a canonical ocean-cube class
implementation_strategy: Create a tiny quality-bearing subset with derivation record if permitted
notes: Do not treat swath and gridded products as equivalent

origin_detail: Ocean-color products exercise skew, masks, packing, and quality metadata
scientific_problem: Validate ocean-color units, missingness, flags, and transformed values
computational_problem: Packed data and provider terms complicate redistribution
why_oceancube: Biogeochemical gridded fields are valid oceancube inputs
implementation_strategy: Derive a tiny subset or a metadata-plus-synthetic fixture after review
notes: CI-safe form depends on redistribution decision

origin_detail: Forcing products test cell methods, long time, and multi-file metadata
scientific_problem: Validate temporal semantics, cell_methods, calendars, and compatibility
computational_problem: Large collections and access terms prohibit naive repository inclusion
why_oceancube: Forcing fields are common upstream covariates
implementation_strategy: Use metadata manifest plus tiny licensed subset or synthetic analogue
notes: Full multi-file use waits for later backend work

origin_detail: Bathymetry is needed for depth orientation and 3-D overlays
scientific_problem: Validate positive direction, units, land/sea masks, bounds, and overlay alignment
computational_problem: Resolution, attribution, and redistribution must be controlled
why_oceancube: Bathymetry supports vertical and visualization contracts
implementation_strategy: Use a coarse attributed subset if license permits
notes: Required before Gate C overlay implementation

origin_detail: Advanced grids need evidence beyond rectilinear center coordinates
scientific_problem: Validate auxiliary coordinates, positions, metrics, and eventually stagger/sigma behavior
computational_problem: Small fixtures must retain topology without large payloads
why_oceancube: Grid semantics are a core oceancube responsibility
implementation_strategy: Start with metadata/topology fixture; add tiny values only after grid contract
prerequisites: Fixture governance and preliminary grid vocabulary
notes: Does not authorize advanced-grid implementation

proposed_api: metadata schema and accessors under review
origin_detail: CF 1.13 defines field and domain semantics needed across providers
scientific_problem: Preserve meaning of variables, axes, coordinates, bounds, measures, mappings, and quality
computational_problem: Attributes are linked objects rather than an unstructured flat list
why_oceancube: CF interpretation is core I/O and metadata work
implementation_strategy: Stage standard_name, long_name, units, coordinates, axis, positive, bounds, cell_methods, cell_measures, grid_mapping, ancillary_variables, flag_values, and flag_masks
dependency_strategy: Native or hybrid engine remains open
notes: Preservation precedes interpretation and validation

origin_detail: Preserved attributes are insufficient without linked semantic interpretation
scientific_problem: Users need to know what a field and its coordinates mean
computational_problem: Partial support can overclaim conformance
why_oceancube: A valid ocean cube requires explicit metadata interpretation
implementation_strategy: Implement preservation, interpretation, validation, advanced-coordinate, then writing stages with declared coverage
dependency_strategy: Compare against ncdfCF as a conformance oracle candidate
notes: Never claim complete CF support from a few attribute checks

proposed_api: CFtime vs internal representation vs alternative
origin_detail: Future julian, noleap, all_leap, and 360_day data cannot be forced into Date safely
scientific_problem: Interpret idealized and historical calendars without false dates
computational_problem: Ordering, grouping, serialization, printing, and arithmetic require a coherent type
why_oceancube: Calendar semantics affect every temporal cube operation
implementation_strategy: Prototype representations and compatibility before extending current calendar support
dependency_strategy: CFtime is a candidate; dependency not selected
prerequisites: CF preservation, time invariants, and DEC-023
notes: Current standard, gregorian, and proleptic_gregorian behavior remains

origin_detail: Depth, height, pressure, sigma, and hybrid coordinates need distinct semantics
scientific_problem: Prevent invalid conversion of parametric coordinates to metric depth
computational_problem: Formula terms and auxiliary variables must be resolved consistently
why_oceancube: Vertical semantics are core physical-field preparation
implementation_strategy: Interpret axis, positive, units, bounds, formula_terms, and required auxiliary variables before conversion
notes: Foundation for Gate B and advanced grids

origin_detail: stars offers labeled N-D geospatial arrays, proxies, and curvilinear metadata
scientific_problem: Exchange data with the R spatial N-D ecosystem
computational_problem: Round trips can lose backend, variable, and provenance semantics
why_oceancube: Optional interoperability belongs at the cube boundary
implementation_strategy: Prototype one-way and round-trip mappings with explicit loss reports
dependency_strategy: Optional Suggests adapter only if approved
notes: stars is not a replacement for ocean_cube

origin_detail: terra provides on-disk SpatRaster and mature raster operations
scientific_problem: Exchange compatible surfaces and layer stacks with raster workflows
computational_problem: Depth/time/variable dimensions and metadata do not map automatically
why_oceancube: Raster/surface interchange is an oceancube boundary concern
implementation_strategy: Define supported dimensional slices and explicit information-loss diagnostics
dependency_strategy: Optional Suggests adapter only if approved
notes: Do not delegate the ocean_cube contract to terra

proposed_api: existing geometry inputs plus converter review
origin_detail: Vector domains, polygons, transects, and CRS need standards-based exchange
scientific_problem: Represent vector geometries and geodetic operations consistently
computational_problem: CRS, s2 behavior, and geometry lifecycles must be explicit
why_oceancube: oceancube already owns field-domain geometry and weights
implementation_strategy: Keep sf optional and use plain keyed outputs where geometry retention is unnecessary
prerequisites: CF grid mapping and geometry invariants
notes: sf is the vector-domain adapter, not the cube storage model

proposed_api: as.data.frame methods or explicit extract arguments under review
origin_detail: Tabular consumers need stable coordinates, indices, units, and provenance keys
scientific_problem: Move profiles, series, sections, and weighted values without hidden objects
computational_problem: Wide and long representations can lose dimensions or duplicate coordinates
why_oceancube: Plain exchange supports users and downstream packages
implementation_strategy: Define versioned schemas and explicit long/wide loss rules
dependency_strategy: Base data.frame first; optional tidy helpers only if justified
prerequisites: Provenance v1 and stable index semantics
notes: Prefer arguments/methods over many export variants

origin_detail: ncdfCF interprets axes, calendars, bounds, measures, grid mappings, and standard names
scientific_problem: Increase CF coverage and detect divergent interpretation
computational_problem: Depending fully on another object model may reduce control over ocean_cube semantics
why_oceancube: CF correctness is core but implementation strategy is open
implementation_strategy: Compare representative files and diagnostics against a bounded native prototype
dependency_strategy: Adapter, oracle, or hybrid dependency selected by evidence
prerequisites: CF fixtures and engine option paper
notes: Do not adopt automatically as the internal engine

origin_detail: Downstream indicators need stable field, geometry, unit, and provenance inputs
scientific_problem: Separate physical-field preparation from indicator calculation
computational_problem: Package coupling and undocumented joins can invalidate analyses
why_oceancube: oceancube owns upstream schema production and spatind consumes it
implementation_strategy: Version keys, dimensions, units, bounds, missingness, provenance links, and compatibility policy
dependency_strategy: Plain data first; optional package integration after downstream review
prerequisites: Provenance v1, CF model, accessible spatind contract
notes: Does not prescribe nonexistent spatind functions

proposed_api: object fields and validation; public API under review
origin_detail: Metric depth, height, pressure, nominal, sigma, and hybrid axes are not interchangeable
scientific_problem: Establish units, positive direction, bounds, monotonicity, and transformation provenance
computational_problem: Every vertical operation depends on consistent orientation and coordinates
why_oceancube: Vertical ocean semantics are a core responsibility
implementation_strategy: Define contract and validation before algorithms
dependency_strategy: CF engine; no extra scientific dependency
prerequisites: Gate B fixtures and CF vertical semantics
notes: No named diagnostic begins before this contract

roadmap_item: Vertical gradient, integration, and mean primitives
proposed_api: candidate composable engine with operation argument
origin_detail: Profiles need bounded field transformations with explicit weights and coordinates
scientific_problem: Compute scientifically traceable derivatives and integrals across depth/pressure
computational_problem: Irregular spacing, bounds, masks, and missingness affect results
why_oceancube: These are field-to-field or field-to-profile operations
implementation_strategy: Design one composable primitive engine before separate convenience APIs
dependency_strategy: Use base numerical methods first; external methods only when justified
notes: Public function count remains undecided

roadmap_item: Vertical interpolation, extrema, and depth-at-value primitives
proposed_api: candidate internal engine plus minimal public surface
origin_detail: Named surfaces need explicit crossings, extrema, and interpolation
scientific_problem: Locate physical features without hidden extrapolation or tie choices
computational_problem: Multiple crossings, gaps, inversions, and edge behavior require diagnostics
why_oceancube: These primitives prepare physical fields and surfaces
implementation_strategy: Define methods, ties, extrapolation, missingness, and returned diagnostics before APIs
notes: Depth-at-value supports isotherm/isopycnal surfaces but is not a named diagnosis

proposed_api: profile-wise adapter; candidate API under review
origin_detail: Density and related thermodynamics require authoritative TEOS-10 equations
scientific_problem: Calculate thermodynamic variables with correct salinity, temperature, pressure, and units
computational_problem: Inputs must be aligned, converted, masked, dispatched, and restored efficiently
why_oceancube: oceancube prepares profiles and provenance while gsw owns equations
implementation_strategy: Validate variables/units, derive allowed pressure inputs, dispatch profile-wise, restore cube, record gsw method/version
dependency_strategy: Optional gsw dependency; never reimplement equations
prerequisites: Vertical contract, CF metadata, and TEOS method review
notes: Exact diagnostic API remains separate

origin_detail: Users need depth surfaces for temperature structures
scientific_problem: Define scientifically defensible thermocline and isotherm criteria
computational_problem: Multiple definitions and vertical resolution create method uncertainty
why_oceancube: Produces physical diagnostics and fields
implementation_strategy: Separate methodological review, diagnostics, uncertainty flags, and provenance
dependency_strategy: No renderer dependency; reuse vertical primitives
prerequisites: Vertical contract, primitives, and real depth fixtures
notes: Names and formulas are not final

origin_detail: MLD is a common physical-ocean surface with temperature and density definitions
scientific_problem: Estimate mixed-layer depth with explicit reference and threshold methods
computational_problem: Formula, reference depth, density inputs, inversions, and gaps change results
why_oceancube: MLD is a physical diagnostic derived from fields
implementation_strategy: Separate scientific review and method-specific validation
dependency_strategy: Use gsw only for required thermodynamics
prerequisites: Vertical primitives, TEOS bridge where needed, and MLD fixtures
notes: No default formula is approved

origin_detail: Density structures require TEOS-aware vertical processing
scientific_problem: Locate density gradients and target density surfaces
computational_problem: Density definition, pressure, crossings, and resolution require explicit rules
why_oceancube: These are physical ocean diagnostics
implementation_strategy: Review methods separately and reuse TEOS plus vertical primitives
notes: Isopycnal depth is a surface product, not an ecological indicator

origin_detail: Salinity-gradient structures are relevant vertical ocean features
scientific_problem: Locate halocline features with explicit salinity and depth semantics
computational_problem: Threshold and extrema definitions vary
why_oceancube: Physical vertical diagnostics belong upstream
implementation_strategy: Separate method review using vertical gradients and extrema
dependency_strategy: No new dependency unless method evidence requires it
notes: Formula and public name are not approved

origin_detail: Oxygen gradients and depth surfaces support biogeochemical workflows
scientific_problem: Locate oxygen transition structures without ecological classification
computational_problem: Units, sensor products, multiple crossings, and hypoxia thresholds differ
why_oceancube: A physical concentration-gradient diagnostic can remain field preparation
implementation_strategy: Method review must separate physical gradient from ecological threshold interpretation
notes: Ecological interpretation remains downstream

origin_detail: Historical roadmap and current cube selections support time-distance/depth views
scientific_problem: Show evolution across one spatial or vertical axis
computational_problem: Axis selection and aggregation must remain explicit
why_oceancube: Visualization of prepared fields belongs in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Return ggplot from explicit 2-D preparation without mutating cube
notes: Candidate name only

origin_detail: T-S diagrams are standard profile and water-mass views
scientific_problem: Plot salinity-temperature relationships with optional density context
computational_problem: Variable alignment, units, pressure, and density contours need clear provenance
why_oceancube: Ocean-specific physical visualization belongs upstream
implementation_strategy: Prepare aligned data and use gsw-derived density only when requested
dependency_strategy: ggplot2 core; optional gsw for TEOS context
notes: Water-mass interpretation is user responsibility

origin_detail: OceanView demonstrates vector field display; users need currents and transport context
scientific_problem: Display aligned components with explicit scale and subsampling
computational_problem: Dense arrows, staggering, and map projection can misrepresent direction
why_oceancube: Visualization follows the vector field contract
implementation_strategy: Prepare aligned vectors and renderer-neutral arrow data before plotting
dependency_strategy: Existing ggplot2 first; optional renderer later
notes: Cannot precede vector alignment

origin_detail: Users requested 3-D maps of thermocline, MLD, isotherm, isopycnal, oxycline, and bathymetry surfaces
scientific_problem: Represent physically meaningful depth surfaces in geographic context
computational_problem: Triangulation, orientation, decimation, missing areas, and renderer coupling need contracts
why_oceancube: oceancube prepares the scientific surface and provenance
implementation_strategy: Define renderer-neutral surface table/mesh plus depth orientation and mask semantics
prerequisites: Named or depth-at-value surface, Gate C, memory policy
notes: Scientific data preparation is independent of ggcube

origin_detail: Moving and fixed slices help inspect volumetric structure
scientific_problem: Place horizontal and vertical sections consistently in 3-D coordinates
computational_problem: Coordinate ratios, ordering, depth direction, and decimation affect interpretation
why_oceancube: oceancube owns section preparation and scientific coordinates
implementation_strategy: Reuse current slice/section extraction and create renderer-neutral scene data
prerequisites: Gate C and surface data contract
notes: Prefer method arguments over multiple exports where possible

proposed_api: candidate isosurface preparation plus renderer method
origin_detail: Isotherm, isopycnal, and oxygen surfaces may require 3-D contour extraction
scientific_problem: Extract interpretable surfaces from bounded volumes
computational_problem: Topology, holes, smoothing, memory, and threshold semantics are complex
why_oceancube: A bounded physical surface is field preparation
implementation_strategy: Prototype bounded contour extraction with decimation and diagnostics
dependency_strategy: Renderer remains optional; contour engine selected later
prerequisites: Gate C, memory estimator, and vertical/grid semantics
notes: Large isosurfaces are a separate deferred item

proposed_api: overlay argument or adapter under review
origin_detail: Depth surfaces need seafloor context
scientific_problem: Align bathymetry, land masks, and ocean surfaces with explicit source and resolution
computational_problem: CRS, resolution, vertical datum, and licensing can differ
why_oceancube: oceancube owns physical scene preparation
implementation_strategy: Require user-supplied or approved fixture bathymetry and record source
prerequisites: Bathymetry fixture, Gate C, and grid alignment
notes: Overlay is optional and must not imply a bundled global dataset

origin_detail: ggcube and rgl offer distinct static, lighting, orbit, animation, OpenGL, and WebGL capabilities
scientific_problem: Render positive-down ocean depth without changing scientific coordinate meaning
computational_problem: Platform, headless CI, HTML embedding, and interaction differ by renderer
why_oceancube: oceancube must define scene data before renderer choice
implementation_strategy: Build a platform matrix and renderer-neutral prototype
dependency_strategy: Optional renderer only; never core-hardwire before decision
notes: Decision must include static export and CI behavior

roadmap_item: Large volume rendering, voxels, isosurfaces, and long animation
origin_detail: Large 3-D views are attractive but exceed current memory and execution contracts
scientific_problem: Explore large ocean volumes without accidental materialization
computational_problem: Decimation, chunk access, frame planning, caching, and rendering costs dominate
why_oceancube: oceancube may prepare bounded data after infrastructure exists
implementation_strategy: Defer until lazy/chunk engine and benchmarks define safe limits
prerequisites: Gate E, chunk planner, memory estimator, and scale benchmark
notes: Not part of the 0.3 small/medium 3-D scope

proposed_api: component metadata; public API under review
origin_detail: u, v, and w variables require component identity, orientation, units, and positions
scientific_problem: Distinguish vector components from unrelated scalar variables
computational_problem: Names, CF standard names, grids, and coordinate orientation vary
why_oceancube: Vector field semantics are core physical-field metadata
implementation_strategy: Define recognition hierarchy, overrides, units, sign, and center/face positions
prerequisites: CF model and preliminary grid positions
notes: Recognition must be overridable and diagnosable

origin_detail: Users need magnitude and direction from aligned components
scientific_problem: Create physical scalar fields with explicit angular convention
computational_problem: Projection, units, missingness, and component staggering affect results
why_oceancube: These are field-to-field physical transformations
implementation_strategy: Operate only after alignment and record direction convention
notes: Public API may be arguments rather than separate functions

origin_detail: Staggered components cannot be combined at different positions
scientific_problem: Interpolate components to a declared common position
computational_problem: Metrics, masks, boundaries, and staggering determine valid interpolation
why_oceancube: Grid-aware field preparation belongs in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Use topology and metric-aware interpolation with diagnostics
prerequisites: Grid topology, metrics, and position contract
notes: No vector calculus before alignment

origin_detail: Three-component flows require vertical units and sign conventions
scientific_problem: Represent and visualize vertical motion consistently with depth coordinates
computational_problem: Vertical velocity may use different units, staggering, and positive direction
why_oceancube: It is part of the physical vector field
implementation_strategy: Integrate w only after vertical and grid position contracts
notes: Does not imply trajectory or particle integration

origin_detail: Rectilinear centers are insufficient for advanced ocean-model grids
scientific_problem: Represent axes, topology, center/face/edge positions, CRS, and mappings
computational_problem: Existing five-axis logical shape must coexist with richer coordinates
why_oceancube: Grid semantics are a core oceancube responsibility
implementation_strategy: Design internal contract and migration path before exposing constructors
dependency_strategy: CF model is foundational; xgcm is reference only
prerequisites: CF grid mapping and nontrivial-grid fixtures
notes: Do not force curvilinear arrays into the current 1-D coordinate fields

proposed_api: metric registry and validation; API under review
origin_detail: Distances, areas, thicknesses, and volumes are required for physical derivatives and integrals
scientific_problem: Use location-aware metrics with explicit units and masks
computational_problem: Metrics vary by position and grid topology
why_oceancube: Geometry and physical weighting belong in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Extend existing area/thickness/volume evidence into a position-aware metric model
notes: Existing rectilinear geometry remains the initial implementation evidence

origin_detail: Fields from different sources need explicit grid/resolution alignment
scientific_problem: Map values between declared source and target grids
computational_problem: Nearest, bilinear, conservative, and area-weighted methods have different invariants
why_oceancube: Explicit field transformation is core oceancube work
implementation_strategy: Start rectilinear, require bounds for conservative methods, record method and coverage
dependency_strategy: Optional adapters may delegate after parity evidence
prerequisites: Grid topology, bounds, metrics, and benchmarks
notes: Candidate names only; resampling semantics must separate space and time

origin_detail: Alignment and grid operations need position-aware interpolation
scientific_problem: Interpolate without hidden extrapolation or boundary assumptions
computational_problem: Irregular, masked, and staggered grids require topology-aware rules
why_oceancube: Field-to-field transformations belong in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Implement explicit source/target positions, method, boundary, and diagnostics
dependency_strategy: Native engine or bounded adapter selected after prototypes
notes: Foundation for vector alignment

origin_detail: Physical gradients and integrals require distances, areas, and thicknesses
scientific_problem: Compute traceable spatial/vertical field transformations
computational_problem: Naive index differences are invalid on nonuniform or staggered grids
why_oceancube: These are physical field transformations
implementation_strategy: Use metric registry and position transitions with unit propagation
notes: Advanced diagnostics depend on these primitives

origin_detail: Masks, partial cells, periodicity, fill, extend, and conservative operations need explicit rules
scientific_problem: Avoid silent edge and partial-cell bias
computational_problem: Boundary behavior can dominate derivatives and interpolation
why_oceancube: oceancube owns geometry, masks, and field transformations
implementation_strategy: Define periodic, fill, extend, missing, partial-cell, and mask policies by operation
notes: Antimeridian is tracked separately

proposed_api: grid adapters and selectors under review
origin_detail: Many ocean models use 2-D auxiliary lon/lat or rotated coordinates
scientific_problem: Represent and subset nonrectilinear horizontal domains correctly
computational_problem: Selection, plotting, bounds, and CRS cannot use independent 1-D axes
why_oceancube: Advanced grids remain core grid semantics
implementation_strategy: Add only after ocean_grid contract and real topology fixtures
dependency_strategy: stars may be adapter; CF grid_mapping required
prerequisites: Gate D, topology, metrics, and CF mappings
notes: Not forced into current lon/lat vector fields

origin_detail: Ocean circulation output commonly staggers scalar and velocity fields
scientific_problem: Align and transform C-grid components without false co-location
computational_problem: Topology, masks, metrics, and boundary positions vary by model
why_oceancube: Ocean-model grid semantics belong in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Start with one documented C-grid fixture and explicit positions
prerequisites: Gate D, metrics, interpolation, vector contract
notes: Other staggering arrangements require separate evidence

proposed_api: coordinate transform engine; API under review
origin_detail: Terrain-following ocean grids require formula terms and dynamic depth mapping
scientific_problem: Convert parametric coordinates to physical depth only with complete formula inputs
computational_problem: Auxiliary fields, time dependence, masks, and interpolation are complex
why_oceancube: Vertical/grid coordinate interpretation is core oceancube work
implementation_strategy: Resolve CF formula terms, compute physical coordinates, then explicitly interpolate if requested
dependency_strategy: OceanView is inspiration; native or hybrid engine undecided
prerequisites: CF vertical semantics, ocean_grid, and real sigma fixture
notes: Never infer missing formula terms

origin_detail: Current general antimeridian handling is outside scope
scientific_problem: Select, crop, intersect, and visualize wrapped ocean domains consistently
computational_problem: Longitude conventions, polygon splitting, and periodic grids interact
why_oceancube: Global ocean grid geometry belongs in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Define normalized intervals, periodic axes, geometry splitting, and provenance
notes: Requires dedicated global fixtures

roadmap_item: Collection metadata compatibility and virtual cube contract
proposed_api: collection descriptor; proposed API under review
origin_detail: Many-file products must be validated before concatenation
scientific_problem: Present compatible files as one logical cube without copying all values
computational_problem: Variables, coordinates, attributes, calendars, and encodings can conflict
why_oceancube: Multi-file I/O is core backend work
implementation_strategy: Define compatibility levels, conflict diagnostics, ordering, and source list
dependency_strategy: No Python dependency; native descriptor first
prerequisites: CF model, backend contract, and provenance v1
notes: A candidate cube_open_collection name is not approved

origin_detail: Operational products are commonly partitioned by time
scientific_problem: Expose one ordered time axis with explicit overlaps and gaps
computational_problem: Duplicates, calendars, variable drift, and file order need rules
why_oceancube: Temporal collection semantics belong in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Validate first, then construct a virtual index; materialize only on request
dependency_strategy: Native implementation; xarray is conceptual reference
notes: Do not silently merge conflicting metadata

origin_detail: Remote scientific services enable bounded access without full downloads
scientific_problem: Read remote subsets under the same cube contract
computational_problem: Network errors, server capabilities, authentication, and reproducibility vary
why_oceancube: Remote ocean I/O belongs in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Add narrow adapters with dry-run, size estimates, retries policy, and source identity
dependency_strategy: Optional backend clients; never force credentials into core
prerequisites: CF model, lazy backend, remote provenance, and access fixtures
notes: No remote implementation before bounded local contract is public

origin_detail: Remote subsets require source URL, dataset version, query, time, and identity
scientific_problem: Reproduce exactly what remote data were requested and returned
computational_problem: Mutable endpoints and server-side transformations obscure lineage
why_oceancube: I/O provenance is a core package responsibility
implementation_strategy: Extend provenance v1 with endpoint, query, response identity, checksums/ETag when available, and access time
notes: Credentials must never be recorded

roadmap_item: Reference-based virtual datasets inspired by kerchunk
origin_detail: Many existing NetCDF/HDF files can form virtual cloud-friendly datasets without copying
scientific_problem: Represent logical collections through byte-range references
computational_problem: Reference specs, codecs, object stores, and R ecosystem maturity create dependency risk
why_oceancube: This is a future backend concept, not a Python core commitment
implementation_strategy: Revisit after native multi-file and lazy abstractions; consider interchange rather than implementation
dependency_strategy: No Python core dependency; optional external tooling only if approved
prerequisites: Multi-file contract, chunks, storage abstraction, and remote provenance
notes: Concept only; not required for 0.5 lazy engine

proposed_api: internal operation nodes and explain/inspect candidate
origin_detail: Deferred transformations need explicit parents, parameters, shapes, and provenance
scientific_problem: Represent pending work without executing or losing scientific semantics
computational_problem: Graph growth, serialization, fusion, and error timing require rules
why_oceancube: Lazy field transformation belongs in oceancube backend architecture
implementation_strategy: Define immutable serializable nodes with predicted dimensions and provenance
dependency_strategy: Native R engine; Dask patterns only
prerequisites: Public lazy backend, provenance, and stable operation contracts
notes: Do not imitate Dask API mechanically

origin_detail: Users need to distinguish planning from materialization
scientific_problem: Preserve lazy chains while making execution explicit
computational_problem: Some operations require global state or materialized intermediates
why_oceancube: Backend execution is core oceancube work
implementation_strategy: Classify operations as blockwise, reduction, shuffle/regrid, or eager-only and expose clear collection points
notes: Existing cube_collect informs but does not settle the full API

proposed_api: internal planner with user-visible plan summary candidate
origin_detail: Chunks must align with storage, operation axes, and memory limits
scientific_problem: Execute larger-than-memory operations predictably
computational_problem: Too-small chunks create graph overhead; too-large chunks exhaust memory
why_oceancube: Storage-aware planning is a core backend responsibility
implementation_strategy: Model source chunks, target blocks, halo needs, intermediate size, and peak memory
dependency_strategy: Native planner; Dask guidance as reference
prerequisites: Operation DAG, benchmarks, and memory profiles
notes: Planner policy must be benchmarked on oceancube operations

origin_detail: Long operations need observable progress and controlled reuse
scientific_problem: Avoid repeated expensive reads while retaining reproducibility
computational_problem: Cache invalidation, source mutation, cancellation, and sensitive paths are risks
why_oceancube: Execution ergonomics belong with the lazy engine
implementation_strategy: Key cache by source identity, operation hash, schema, and package version; make progress optional
dependency_strategy: Minimal native interface; optional progress backend only if justified
notes: No implicit persistent cache in the package directory

origin_detail: Independent chunks can reduce wall time for large operations
scientific_problem: Use available compute without changing scientific results
computational_problem: File handles, serialization, memory multiplication, ordering, and cancellation are complex
why_oceancube: Parallelism belongs under the execution contract, not individual functions
implementation_strategy: Start bounded and deterministic; benchmark sequential versus parallel and cap memory
dependency_strategy: Optional R parallel backend selected later; no Dask dependency
prerequisites: Chunk planner, stress tests, and deterministic reductions
notes: Parallel is not automatically faster

proposed_api: candidate cube_write or method; API undecided
origin_detail: Users need reproducible export of transformed cubes
scientific_problem: Write data, coordinates, bounds, metadata, provenance, and quality without semantic loss
computational_problem: Encoding, fill values, unlimited dimensions, groups, and conformance are complex
why_oceancube: NetCDF storage is a core oceancube responsibility
implementation_strategy: Design writer from the stable CF model and round-trip conformance tests
prerequisites: CF stages 1-4, provenance, and writer fixtures
notes: Writing is CF stage 5, not an early metadata shortcut

origin_detail: Storage layout controls size and read performance
scientific_problem: Choose encodings suited to expected ocean selections
computational_problem: Poor chunks or compression can make reads inefficient or lossy
why_oceancube: oceancube writes and reads multidimensional storage
implementation_strategy: Benchmark chunk shapes, compression levels, packing, checksums, and round trips
notes: Lossy packing must be explicit

origin_detail: Zarr provides versioned chunked compressed N-D storage for cloud/object systems
scientific_problem: Access and store large analysis-ready arrays by chunk
computational_problem: R implementation maturity, metadata conventions, codecs, and version compatibility are risks
why_oceancube: A future storage backend fits the cube abstraction
implementation_strategy: Prototype only after CF, lazy, chunk, and storage contracts; declare experimental coverage
dependency_strategy: Optional backend dependency; no Python core
prerequisites: Gate E, writer abstraction, chunk planner, and CF encoding
notes: Zarr container alone does not provide CF/geospatial semantics

origin_detail: Large archives increasingly live in object storage
scientific_problem: Read only required chunks close to data
computational_problem: Authentication, cost, consistency, retries, and provider APIs vary
why_oceancube: Remote storage belongs behind the backend contract
implementation_strategy: Add one bounded optional adapter after local and HTTP/reference contracts are stable
prerequisites: Gate E, remote provenance, and Zarr/reference decision
notes: Never record credentials

origin_detail: In-situ profiles are not naturally rectilinear five-axis cubes
scientific_problem: Represent ragged or sampled vertical observations without false gridding
computational_problem: Variable profile levels and ragged arrays need a distinct contract
why_oceancube: Ocean data interoperability may extend beyond gridded cubes
implementation_strategy: Evaluate CF discrete sampling geometry and oce profile workflows
dependency_strategy: Optional adapters; do not overload ocean_cube prematurely
prerequisites: Stable gridded contracts and DSG fixtures
notes: Could remain an adapter rather than a core class

origin_detail: Drifters and moving platforms have observation-indexed coordinates
scientific_problem: Preserve moving coordinates, time, variables, and quality
computational_problem: A rectilinear cube would misrepresent trajectory topology
why_oceancube: Potential ocean-data extension requires a distinct model
implementation_strategy: Evaluate CF trajectory DSG and exchange with tabular/spatial tools
prerequisites: Stable provenance, time, and DSG contract
notes: Lagrangian simulation remains out of scope

proposed_api: ensemble axis or collection metadata; API under review
origin_detail: Forecast and model products may include members beyond the canonical axes
scientific_problem: Represent member identity and aggregation without treating members as variables
computational_problem: Logical shape, metadata, lazy reads, and statistics need compatibility rules
why_oceancube: Ensemble ocean fields are upstream data representation
implementation_strategy: Prototype as explicit auxiliary dimension or collection after core contracts stabilize
notes: Do not silently repurpose variable axis

origin_detail: CF defines feature types for point, timeSeries, profile, and trajectory observations
scientific_problem: Interpret observation collections using their actual sampling geometry
computational_problem: Contiguous/indexed ragged arrays and instance dimensions require specialized logic
why_oceancube: CF-aware data access may include non-gridded ocean observations
implementation_strategy: Implement adapter contracts only after gridded 1.0 foundations are near stable
notes: Not required for 0.3 or 0.4

origin_detail: Some ocean models use connectivity-based meshes
scientific_problem: Represent cells, nodes, faces, connectivity, and metrics without false rectilinear axes
computational_problem: Topology and algorithms differ fundamentally from current grids
why_oceancube: Could be a long-term ocean grid extension
implementation_strategy: Evaluate UGRID and adapter-first feasibility after advanced structured grids
dependency_strategy: Optional mesh ecosystem adapter preferred before core expansion
prerequisites: Stable ocean_grid, CF model, metrics, and fixtures
notes: May remain outside core if maintenance cost is excessive

origin_detail: Function produces indicators and ocean_indicators objects
scientific_problem: Maintain compatibility while restoring package boundary
computational_problem: Immediate removal would break users and downstream replacement does not yet exist
why_oceancube: Migration must be coordinated from oceancube to spatind
implementation_strategy: Retain unchanged; define downstream parity, migration, deprecation, and release timeline later
prerequisites: Equivalent downstream implementation and maintainer approval
notes: No deprecation, migration, or removal is authorized

origin_detail: Stock-oriented naming may encode downstream domain semantics
scientific_problem: Determine whether behavior is generic geometry or indicator-specific preparation
computational_problem: Consumers and replacement parity are unknown
why_oceancube: Geometry can belong in oceancube but stock interpretation may not
implementation_strategy: Audit semantics and consumers individually; do not infer from name
prerequisites: Accessible spatind contract and usage evidence
notes: Not an automatic migration candidate

origin_detail: Stock-oriented crop semantics require boundary classification
scientific_problem: Separate generic field cropping from downstream stock workflow convenience
computational_problem: Behavior and external consumers may rely on compatibility
why_oceancube: Selection belongs upstream but domain wrappers need review
implementation_strategy: Audit behavior, redundancy, and consumers before any lifecycle proposal
notes: No deprecation is authorized

origin_detail: Linking events may be field extraction or downstream analytical joining depending on semantics
scientific_problem: Clarify stable upstream matching versus indicator/event interpretation
computational_problem: Temporal/spatial matching and downstream meaning may be mixed
why_oceancube: Explicit extraction can belong in oceancube
implementation_strategy: Audit contract and consumers before deciding retain, generalize, or migrate
notes: Not an automatic migration candidate

origin_detail: Name suggests generic signal-to-noise but behavior is standardized anomaly magnitude or signed z
scientific_problem: Avoid scientific misinterpretation while preserving compatibility
computational_problem: Renaming or deprecation can fragment established workflows
why_oceancube: Current behavior is a field transformation but the name is ambiguous
implementation_strategy: Keep behavior documented; evaluate alias or terminology only in a separate lifecycle review
prerequisites: Usage evidence and API lifecycle policy
notes: No deprecation is authorized

origin_detail: Released tests and documentation define elapsed-time ordinary linear slope
scientific_problem: Describe per-cell field change without claiming inference
computational_problem: Adding significance or robust trend methods would cross the package boundary
why_oceancube: Descriptive field slope remains a field-to-field operation
implementation_strategy: Preserve current contract and direct inferential requests downstream
notes: Historical Theil-Sen proposal is superseded by DEC-026

roadmap_item: Upgrade Pages checkout action from v4
origin_detail: Pages uses actions/checkout@v4 while R-CMD-check uses v5
scientific_problem: Keep workflow actions aligned and maintained
computational_problem: Workflow changes can affect Pages but not scientific behavior
why_oceancube: Repository infrastructure supports oceancube publication
implementation_strategy: Upgrade in a separate low-risk workflow commit with Pages verification
notes: Do not edit workflow in roadmap phase

roadmap_item: Populate GitHub description, homepage, and topics
origin_detail: Repository metadata fields are empty
scientific_problem: Improve discovery and accurately describe the released package
computational_problem: Metadata can overclaim scope if not release-aligned
why_oceancube: Repository presentation belongs to project maintenance
implementation_strategy: Apply audited short description, canonical homepage, and focused topics separately
notes: Not core 0.3 scientific work

origin_detail: GitHub reports NOASSERTION while DESCRIPTION declares MIT plus LICENSE
scientific_problem: Make legal terms machine-recognizable and complete
computational_problem: The current R license stub may be insufficient for GitHub detection
why_oceancube: Clear licensing is project governance
implementation_strategy: Review copyright holder/year and standard MIT text in a separate legal-metadata commit
notes: Do not guess legal metadata

roadmap_item: Reconcile duplicate and historically stale documentation surfaces
origin_detail: Handbook Rmd/md, vignette, Quarto, generated docs, and historical roadmap overlap
scientific_problem: Keep one source of truth per purpose without losing scientific context
computational_problem: Deletion before parity can discard unique material and break links
why_oceancube: Documentation architecture is part of package maintenance
implementation_strategy: Add status notices and consolidate gradually after topic-level parity approval
prerequisites: Documentation map, link audit, and owner approval
notes: No historical file is deleted by this roadmap

roadmap_item: Resolve merged dev-0.2.0 and future dev-0.3.0 branch policy
origin_detail: dev-0.2.0 is fully merged and no 0.3 development branch should exist before Gate A
scientific_problem: Keep branch names aligned with active development
computational_problem: Premature deletion or branch creation obscures release state
why_oceancube: Repository workflow supports controlled oceancube development
implementation_strategy: Approve policy, then delete merged branch and create dev-0.3.0 only when development starts
notes: No branch action occurs in roadmap phase

origin_detail: Occupied area/volume, center of gravity, dispersion, inertia, Gini, entropy, hotspots, fragmentation, overlap, compression, and shifts are downstream outputs
scientific_problem: Calculate interpretable spatial indicators from prepared fields and weights
computational_problem: Indicator definitions and uncertainty are not cube transformations
why_oceancube: oceancube should supply fields, weights, keys, and provenance only
implementation_strategy: Define in downstream package using versioned exchange schema
dependency_strategy: No oceancube dependency beyond shared contract
notes: No movement of existing functions occurs in this phase

roadmap_item: Indicator trend inference, breakpoints, and regimes
origin_detail: Sen slope, Mann-Kendall, p-values, uncertainty, change points, and regimes apply to indicator series
scientific_problem: Quantify indicator change and uncertainty
computational_problem: Inferential assumptions and ecological interpretation exceed field transformation
why_oceancube: oceancube stops at descriptive per-cell field slope
implementation_strategy: Implement downstream with explicit methods and uncertainty
dependency_strategy: No oceancube scientific dependency beyond exchange
notes: cube_trend must not expand into these methods

roadmap_item: Stock assessment, species/community models, machine learning, and causal inference
origin_detail: Historical scope excludes general modeling and inference frameworks
scientific_problem: These analyses consume prepared ocean fields but require separate domain models
computational_problem: Model training, validation, interpretation, and governance are distinct systems
why_oceancube: Keeping them out preserves a focused package contract
implementation_strategy: Provide interoperable outputs rather than implementations
notes: No public stubs or roadmap exports

origin_detail: Trajectory simulation is not part of the field transformation baseline
scientific_problem: Particle advection requires numerical integration and model-specific velocity handling
computational_problem: Time stepping, interpolation, boundaries, diffusion, and uncertainty form a separate engine
why_oceancube: oceancube may prepare velocity fields but should not become a particle model
implementation_strategy: Expose validated vector fields for specialized tools
notes: Observed trajectory data may still be an adapter candidate under OC-DATA-02
